Release notes

What changed in each build we put on TestFlight before the public release, in plain words.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (17) · 2026-10-31

Build 17: Drifting Ship

This build went up on TestFlight on October 31, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 16, plus the changes below.

  • Sea 13, the Drifting Ship: 8 new stages. The third star on these stages is for dodging the drifting ship.
  • The Ink button now pauses the game and opens a Harbor pop-up. The item slots in the Harbor (four of them) will open soon.
  • The most Ink you can use in one stage now goes up by one per volume: 5 in Volume One, 6 in Volume Two.
  • In boss seas Ink's effects are weaker, and the game now tells you so.
  • Ink feels better in the boss stage of 7-8.
  • Stage 13-3 has been rebalanced.
  • Korean text wrapping and speech bubbles have been refined.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (16) · 2026-10-31

Build 16: Twin Isles

This build went up on TestFlight on October 31, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 15, plus the changes below.

  • Sea 12, Twin Isles, the second sea of Volume Two: 8 new stages.
  • A new rule, twin isles: two paired islands grow faster when one owner holds both, and both stop growing when the owner changes.
  • A celadon-tinted morning sea.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (15) · 2026-10-31

Build 15: Beyond the Chart, and the Reef

This build went up on TestFlight on October 31, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 14, plus the changes below.

  • Volume Two, Beyond the Chart, begins. Sea 11, Clear Water: 8 new stages. Past the edge of the map lies a white sea, and you draw it with your own ink.
  • A new element at sea, the reef: a ship cannot pierce a reef and sails around its edge. When you drag, the path it will take around the reef shows ahead of time.
  • The Volume Two seas look like a paper sea chart: white paper by day, black paper by night.
  • The sea name at the top of the chart no longer hides behind the routes.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (14) · 2026-10-31

Build 14: First Light, and the End of Volume One

This build went up on TestFlight on October 31, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 13, plus the changes below.

  • Sea 10, First Light: 8 new stages. With them, Volume One is complete: 10 seas, 80 stages.
  • The ending of Volume One: the first time you win the last stage, the colour of the sea spreads across the chart and the lighthouse is lit. You can watch it again from the Sea 10 chart.
  • Numbers on light-coloured islands are easier to read.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (13) · 2026-10-31

Build 13: Whirlpool Sea, Open Sea and Night Sea

This build went up on TestFlight on October 31, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 12, plus the changes below.

  • Sea 7, the Whirlpool Sea: 8 new stages. A fleet that passes through a whirlpool loses one in five. Open alliances appear.
  • Sea 8, the Open Sea: 8 new stages. It mixes in elements from the seas you have already crossed.
  • Sea 9, the Night Sea: at set times your sight narrows and only the area around lighthouses is visible. 8 new stages.
  • Each sea now has its own look, and stage balance has been refined.
  • A preview of Sea 10, First Light: its stages are in, but its look is not yet.
  • Fixed Ink being counted twice in some cases. A copy restored from a backup now gets its own device identity.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (12) · 2026-10-31

Build 12: Current Way and the Coral Reef

This build went up on TestFlight on October 31, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 11, plus the changes below.

  • Sea 4, Current Way: 8 new stages. Currents push your fleets along or hold them back, and they reverse every 30 seconds. Ships leaving a harbor island travel 1.5 times faster. Allied fleets appear.
  • Sea 5, the Coral Reef: 8 new stages. A coral island you hold grows faster every 20 seconds, and starts over if it is taken. An island left untouched for 8 seconds grows 1.25 times faster, shown as a slow ring of ripples.
  • Sea 6, the Tidal Flats: 8 new stages. On a tide schedule, sandbars sink at high tide and surface at low tide.
  • Fleet dots and troop labels no longer cover the numbers on islands. The ends of current bands fade out like spreading ink. Whirlpools get a label, and there is a new HUD for allies.
  • Ink can be used up to 3 times per stage. Its effects run one at a time.
  • Fixed lighthouse information showing through the fog.
  • Fixed the Ink count not matching when you continue across devices through iCloud.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (11) · 2026-10-31

Build 11: the Fog Isles, language choice and leaderboards

This build went up on TestFlight on October 31, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 10, plus the changes below.

  • Sea 3, the Fog Isles: 8 new stages. Numbers beyond the fog show the last value you saw, dimmed, and lighting a lighthouse lets you see farther. Enemies that build up strength inside the fog appear.
  • Each sea now has its own sea color.
  • Each sea shows three lines of story.
  • You can choose the language in settings: 12 languages, or follow the device. On iOS, the per-app language setting works too.
  • The first time you start, you choose a nickname.
  • Game Center leaderboards. Runs where you used Ink are not ranked.
  • Fixed stage titles being cut off, and fixed the header of the sea chart.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (10) · 2026-10-30

Build 10: a livelier capture, with ink spreading and a soft haptic

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 9, plus the changes below.

  • Capturing an island now spreads ink over it in 0.65 seconds, with a small ink ring and a brief press on the number. When an island is taken from you, the spread is darker and shorter (0.42 seconds).
  • When you capture an island, the phone gives a light haptic tap. If Reduce Motion is on, only the color changes, with no spreading.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (9) · 2026-10-30

Build 9: box-select only, fleets above islands

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 8, plus the changes below.

  • Selecting several islands is now done only by dragging a rectangle over open sea. The old gesture of dragging through islands one by one is gone, because the path could easily tangle when played fast. Dragging from one island to a target still works.
  • Fleets and their paths are now always drawn above every island, whether neutral, yours or the enemy’s, so a ship is never hidden under an island.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (8) · 2026-10-30

Build 8: serif titles and a paper grain

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 7, plus the changes below.

  • The wordmark, the result titles and the new-sea notice now use two serif typefaces (Cinzel and Cormorant Garamond, both under the SIL Open Font License). They apply to Latin and Cyrillic text; other writing systems keep the system typeface.
  • A faint paper grain now lies over the chart, so the painted sea reads as ink on paper.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (7) · 2026-10-30

Build 7: a gentler Ink and iCloud resume

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 6, plus the changes below.

  • Ink is weaker and shorter: troops grow about 1.33 times faster for 30 seconds (before: 1.5 times for 45 seconds). On sea boss stages it is a little weaker still, about 1.25 times, and a short notice says so.
  • iCloud resume: your stars, best times, unlocked stages and the Ink you earned in play carry over to your other devices signed in to the same iCloud account, with nothing to sign in to or export. If iCloud is off or signed out, the app keeps working on the device as before.
  • Supporting the game gives no advantage in play. It only adds a thank-you mark.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (6) · 2026-10-30

Build 6: a danger warning, Ink and 12 languages

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 5, plus the changes below.

  • Danger warning: when you are about to lose within about 10 seconds and one Ink could still save the round, the game slows down, then stops and asks "Use Ink" or "Continue". It happens at most once per round, and it can be turned off in settings.
  • The item that was called tide is now called Ink, in all 12 languages.
  • Stages 1-1 to 1-4 now play without Ink: no Ink button and no danger warning. The difficulty is tuned from 1-5 on, and your first clear of 1-5 gives you 2 Ink as a gift.
  • The app's own texts now come in all 12 languages of this site. A device language outside those 12 shows English.
  • iPad: the screen is now filled edge to edge, with larger interface elements, and the battle map spreads out sideways.
  • A quiet "Support" entry now appears on the results screen of every stage and in the pause menu. Nothing pops up during a battle.
  • Supporting the game gives no advantage in play. It only adds a thank-you mark.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (5) · 2026-10-30

Build 5: a new supporter card

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 4, plus the changes below.

  • A new supporter card design, laid out like a nautical chart window.
  • The time of day and the border change with the supporter's tier.
  • The card can be shared to social media.
  • Supporting the game gives no advantage in play. It only adds a thank-you mark.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (4) · 2026-10-30

Build 4: tide items, in-app purchases and a difficulty pass

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 to 3, plus the changes below.

  • Tide items, a new kind of item you can use in battle.
  • In-app purchases: tide items in packs of 5 and 15, and a supporter option.
  • Restore purchases.
  • Difficulty adjusted.
  • Fixed the -N numbers overlapping each other.
  • Supporting the game gives no advantage in play. It only adds a thank-you mark.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (3) · 2026-10-30

Build 3: a new look, new sounds and new ways to play

This build went up on TestFlight on October 30, 2026. It has the contents of builds 1 and 2, plus the changes below.

  • A newly made intro that follows the time of day, day or night, about 15 to 20 seconds long.
  • A new look: a watercolor sea, islands with depth, spreading ink, and backgrounds that change with the time of day.
  • Sound effects, and a background sound of waves.
  • When two fleets' paths overlap, their troops cancel each other out.
  • Drag a rectangle to select several islands at once, and quick drags are easier to make.
  • A settings button, and the release notes now open inside the app in a web view.
  • A progress bar along the top of the screen.
  • Fleets now leave as an ink drop with a dotted tail.

On TestFlight 1.0.0 (2) · 2026-10-29

Build 2: first TestFlight build

This build went up on TestFlight on October 29, 2026. It has the contents of build 1, plus the fix below.

  • Fixed: on the very first stage the map (the islands) did not show and the screen was empty. The islands now appear.
  • More careful checks before release: before each upload, the real app is now run automatically up to the first stage.

Preparing for TestFlight 1.0.0 (1)

Build 1: getting ready for TestFlight

Build 1 was never uploaded. Its contents went out in build 2, the first TestFlight build; this entry keeps what was planned for it.

  • A sea chart with 16 stages in two seas. Tap a stage to see its goal and the stars you have.
  • Battles by dragging: pull from your island to send troops, and captured islands fill with spreading ink.
  • Up to three stars per stage. Your progress is saved on the phone, and stars never go down.
  • Three different ten-second intros (sky, sea and land). You can skip them, and they get shorter after the first few times.
  • If the phone's reduce-motion setting is on, the intro, the screen changes and the chart effects stop moving. Effects during a battle are not affected.
  • Soft sounds that the app makes itself. Sound is off by default.
  • A new app icon: a coral ink island on cream.
  • An information screen with the app version and a link to the privacy policy.
  • Smoother play between stages: a short result sheet, a preview of the next stage, and a marker when you missed a star by only a little.
  • A teaser for the next sea, which is not playable yet.
  • When you come back to the chart after a stage, the next stage glows softly for a moment, then the glow goes away. It does not show if reduce-motion is on.
  • Leaving a stage with the phone's back button or swipe gesture also brings you back to the chart with the right effect.
  • Not checked yet: the app has not been run on a real iPhone or Android phone from a store build.
